description: Data scientist / ML engineer working on a churn model. Jargon-dense (AUC, feature store, leakage), reflective about mistakes (self-corrections on metrics), methodical.

messages.text: We decided to use a gradient-boosted tree instead of the neural net for the churn model, way easier to explain to stakeholders.
Decision: features get versioned in the feature store, no more ad-hoc CSV pulls.
We're using Optuna for hyperparameter search on the ranking model.
Requirement: every model artifact must log its training data hash for reproducibility.
We can't use raw user IDs as a feature, that's a leakage risk the privacy review flagged.
Actually, the validation AUC was 0.81, not 0.86 like I reported this morning, I had a leak in the split.
The correct value for the learning rate in the final run is 0.003.
We tried oversampling the minority class but it didn't work, it just overfit to duplicates.
Failed approach: manual feature selection by eyeballing correlations, missed interaction effects.
Check notebooks/churn_eda.ipynb for the exploratory analysis.
See https://wandb.ai/acme/churn-model/runs/xyz for the full run comparison — I just call it 'the dashboard run' when I mention it in meetings.
I always want a held-out test set that never touches the notebook, only the pipeline.
